## Requirements (contract § In scope)

1. `apply_withdrawals` emits `withdrawn_routes.conf` covering `/<route>/`,
   `/<route>/index.html`, the no-slash form and the `.json` form of every
   denied route; nginx answers **410 with the `sig.tombstone/1` body**
   (target_kind, target_id, withdrawn_at, public-safe reason_class,
   disposition_ref, superseded_by, release label, corrections link — never
   an embedded e-mail).
2. Entity stubs + `page_index` pages are covered and generated from the
   same deny set (no hand-maintained second list).
3. `/r/<pub>/` gets a landing page (with meta description) — never 403.
4. Tests: composed/nginx proof of 410+tombstone on every alias of a
   withdrawn fixture route; a `_route_targets` unit test proving alias
   completeness from the deny set.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] every alias of a withdrawn fixture route → 410 + valid `sig.tombstone/1` body, composed stack (staging-verified)
- [ ] alias completeness + entity-stub generation unit-tested from a deny set (fixture-verified)
- [ ] `/r/<pub>/` landing with meta description, not 403 (fixture-verified)
- [ ] no tombstone/stub contains an e-mail address (engineered — test)
- [ ] verification green: `make check`; invariants not living records; ids stamped; DEFERRALS row for the unverifiable; ADR for deviations (engineered)
- [ ] head-bound CI read via `docs/build/tools/ci_boundary.py`; 5 required checks; `ci:` line recorded (engineered)
- [ ] one-commit closeout after the PR exists: run ledger, `pr/P34.41.md`, BUILD_INDEX row, LEDGER advance, README rows line (engineered)
- [ ] record rules: verdict-word/ext record rules, protected records append-only, `memory_guard all --staged` green (engineered)

## Plan

- `exports/src/exports/release_pages.py` — `_layout()` gains an optional
  `<meta name="description">`; new `namespace_landing(entry)` renders the
  `/r/<pub>/` index (namespace orientation: compartment links, manifest +
  descriptor + landing links); `tombstone_page()` gains the full
  `sig.tombstone/1` field set (target kind/id, withdrawn_at, reason class,
  disposition_ref, superseded_by, release label, corrections link); the
  entity-stub tombstone reuses it.
- `exports/src/exports/release.py` — `_route_targets` yields
  `(kind, target_id, rel_path, shape)` (page|file) and gains the
  `/entity/<t>/<id>/` stub routes; `apply_withdrawals` computes a single
  deny set split page-vs-file routes, folds in the claim/release rules
  (release deny also globs `s/<pub>`/`v/<pub>`), denies stub routes when
  their entity is denied or their active-release record route is denied,
  scans every `page_index.json` and denies + marks each page embedding a
  denied id; materialises tombstone pages (dirs), `sig.tombstone/1` JSON
  bodies (`.json` files), removes other denied bytes whole, writes
  per-route tombstone bodies under `conf/tombstone/<sha24>.{html,json}` and
  emits `location =` exact-match denies for **every alias**
  (`/<route>`, `/<route>/`, `/<route>/index.html`; `/<route>` for file
  routes) each carrying `error_page 410 /conf/tombstone/<h>` so the 410
  serves the route's own tombstone body — never the generic nginx page.
  `route_access` learns the `entity/<t>/<id>` stub routes (entity deny, or
  the active release's record route denied via claim/release). `_entity_
  overlay` emits the tombstone stub for deny-set entities (passed the set
  from `apply_withdrawals`). `build_release` emits `r/<pub>/index.html` =
  `namespace_landing`.
- `ops/web/nginx.conf` — `location /conf/tombstone/ { internal; }` (the
  body files are error_page internals, never public routes).
- `ops/src/ops/release_serving.py` — `apply` passes the registry's latest
  pub as `active_pub` so stub denies follow the pointer.
- `ops/README.md` — the runbook note names the new conf shape +
  `conf/tombstone/` bodies.
- Tests: `tests/exports/test_release.py` + `tests/ops/test_release_serving.py`
  unit rows; `tests/e2e/test_serving_topology.py` gains the real
  `apply`-on-the-served-tree alias proof (Docker-gated, staging-verified).

**MET-DIFFERENTLY / deviations:** none requiring an ADR — every change
implements the contract verbatim. Two additive extensions worth naming:
(a) a release deny also globs the `s/<pub>`/`v/<pub>` snapshot namespaces
(contract names `r/`+`releases/`; the namespaces are the same release's
bytes and the deny map already dominates them via `route_access`); (b)
`superseded_by` is always `null` today — the *effective* disposition is by
definition current, so no successor is known at deny time (field emitted,
populated when a successor mechanism exists).
